instantiated_cells.justification: Section 13.74(1) requires the ethics commission to examine all statements filed under the subchapter and note discrepancies, and § 13.685(3) requires the commission to examine each expense statement filed under § 13.68 — this constitutes a mandatory compliance review by the regulator rather than a regular independent third-party audit, best matching the MODERATE criterion.

arguments.justification: Section 13.69 prescribes forfeitures up to $5,000 for principals and $1,000 for lobbyists violating ss. 13.61–13.68, criminal penalties (fine up to $1,000 or up to one year in jail) for falsified statements, and Class H felony for knowingly filing false statements under ss. 13.63, 13.64, 13.65, 13.67 or 13.68, covering registration failures, late or false reports.

content.text:
I'll analyze the statute text for both cells.

**Row 001 (penalties):** § 13.69 clearly establishes penalties — forfeitures for principals ($5,000), lobbyists ($1,000), Class H felony for false statements, license revocation, etc.

**Row 002 (audits):** § 13.74 requires the commission to examine all statements filed and may examine supporting documents. This is a compliance review requirement by the ethics commission (the regulator), not necessarily an "impartial third party" audit. § 13.685(3) also requires examination of each statement. This appears to be a mandatory compliance review rather than an independent third-party audit — best matches MODERATE.
